summary: The PR changes only production code (SSTable.delete now deletes components oldest-first by mtime and calls FileUtils.delete instead of deleteWithConfirm). It adds no tests, although the ticket's test plan promises additions to LogTransactionTest. None of the changed behaviours is tested: the crash-recovery scenario, the deletion order, and the changed failure contract. Coverage: 0/3 changed behaviours have a test that would catch a regression.

findings.problem: The PR adds or changes no tests, even though the ticket's test plan says 'additions to LogTransactionTest'. The point of the fix is that a partially completed deletion keeps the sstable's maximum mtime unchanged, so LogFile.verifyRecord still accepts the REMOVE record on restart. Nothing tests this. Going back to DATA-first or arbitrary-order deletion would pass the current suite. The existing mtime tests (testStatsTSMismatchDuringStart, testWrongTimestampInTxnFile, testStatsTSMismatchDuringList) only cover a newer STATS file, which verifyRecord ignores. They never cover a newer non-STATS component, such as DATA or an index file, combined with a partial delete.
findings.fix: Add a LogTransactionTest case. Build an sstable and use setLastModified to give its components distinct mtimes, with DATA or another non-STATS component as the newest; allow at least a 1s gap because of mtime truncation. Write the REMOVE record with log.obsoleted(sstable). Then simulate a crash partway through: delete only the oldest k components in the order SSTable.delete would use, or make one later component undeletable with a read-only parent directory or a component whose deletion fails. Assert that LogTransaction.removeUnfinishedLeftovers / listFiles(OnTxnErr.THROW) succeeds and that all leftover components are removed. Also add a negative check: deleting the newest component first fails verification. That shows the test is sensitive to deletion order.

findings.problem: In production, SSTable.delete is reached through SSTableTidier.run. The tidier deletes the DATA file itself first, without regard to mtime, and only then calls SSTable.delete(desc, discoverComponentsFor(desc)). So in the ticket's crash scenario the first file removed is still DATA. If DATA is the newest component, the maximum mtime changes immediately. A test that calls SSTable.delete directly would pass while the scenario from the ticket is still possible. The effect that matters is what happens on disk after the tidier runs and the node restarts, and nothing covers that path.
findings.fix: Run the regression test from TR-1 through the real path: commit the transaction so the SSTableTidier runs, with an interrupted or failed deletion partway through. Do not call SSTable.delete directly. The test must make DATA the newest component. That is the case this test would expose if the tidier's own DATA-first delete still breaks the guarantee.

findings.problem: The failure behaviour has changed without a test. Before, every component except SUMMARY was removed with FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws on failure. SSTableTidier.run catches that exception and adds the tidier to failedDeletions so the deletion is retried. Now FileUtils.delete returns false and the result is ignored. When a component fails to delete, the failure is silently dropped, no retry is scheduled, and the parentRef is released, which can leave orphaned files behind. No test pins either the old behaviour or the new one.
findings.fix: Add a test where a non-DATA component cannot be deleted, for example a read-only directory or a non-empty directory with that component's name. Assert the intended contract: either SSTableTidier records a failed deletion and retries it (rescheduleFailedDeletions / failedDeletions is non-empty), or the leftover is cleaned up on removeUnfinishedLeftovers. If the silent loss is a regression, the test will fail and expose it.
